children: Collins Aerospace business expanded its commercial aviation aftermarket operations through new agreements with ST Engineering and Royal Brunei Airlines, extending its role in aircraft component repair and long-term maintenance support.

Collins and ST Engineering signed three multi-year agreements covering component repairs, spare parts and lifecycle support for Boeing 787, 737 and Airbus A320-family aircraft. Financial terms weren’t disclosed.

Under the agreements, ST Engineering will repair Collins fan assembly electronics boards used on the Boeing 787, with the companies aiming to shorten turnaround times by repairing components rather than replacing them.

ST Engineering also expanded an existing agreement to purchase Collins Power & Controls spare parts for its component maintenance, repair and overhaul operations. The expanded arrangement adds narrowbody aircraft components to ST Engineering’s repair portfolio.
The companies also extended their collaboration on line replaceable unit repairs for Airbus A320 and Boeing 737-family aircraft through Collins’ FlightSense aftermarket support program.
Separately, Collins secured two 12-year contracts with Royal Brunei Airlines covering the carrier’s current and future Boeing 787 fleet.

The agreements cover Collins’ FlightSense and Dispatch services for systems including avionics, cargo, electrical power, environmental controls and lighting. The programs provide component availability and maintenance support under a fixed-rate service model.

Collins will also provide predictive maintenance, logistics support and access to spare and repaired parts. FlightSense uses the company’s Ascentia analytics platform to analyze aircraft data and identify maintenance needs.

For RTX investors, the agreements add to Collins Aerospace’s long-duration commercial aftermarket business, which generates recurring revenue from maintenance, parts and support after aircraft and components enter service. The 12-year Royal Brunei contracts in particular extend Collins’ aftermarket exposure to the Boeing 787 fleet in the Asia-Pacific region.
